beats.text: More sex, happier couple? Only up to a point.
Researchers looked at surveys from over thirty thousand Americans.
For people in relationships, well-being rose with sex, up to about once a week.
After that, more didn't make people any happier.
And for singles, there was no link at all.
It doesn't prove cause and effect. Happier couples may simply have more sex.
So stop counting. Staying connected matters more than the number.

sources: Muise, Schimmack & Impett (2016). Sexual frequency predicts greater well-being, but more is not always better. Social Psychological and Personality Science 7(4). Three studies, >30,000 Americans; well-being associated with frequency up to about once a week, no further gain beyond; no association for singles; correlational. Via Medical News Today.
